newsitem.title: BRAZIL: France's Chirac arrives in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac arrives in Brazil.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac arrived in the Brazilian capital on Tuesday, kicking off a week-long tour of five South American nations aimed at boosting trade with the region.
Chirac touched down in Brasilia and was later scheduled to have a private dinner with Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.

Chirac has made no bones about his intention to challenge U.S. dominance in the region and plead for the Mercosur customs union, South America's emerging economic power, to stake its future on the European Union rather than a proposed all-America free trade area.

His longest foreign tour since taking office nearly two years ago will also take him to the three other Mercosur countries, Uruguay, Paraguay and Argentina, as well as Bolivia, which is linked to the group by a free trade accord.
He announced plans for another Latin American tour likely to include Mexico early next year. President Bill Clinton is due to visit Mexico next month and Brazil and Argentina in May.

France wants to put flesh on a basic agreement signed between the EU and Mercosur in order to delay the proposed American free trade area, which the southern group is in no hurry to join. But Brasilia will ask for a price -- that France use its influence in the EU to lower trade barriers to imports from Brazil.
The daily O Estado de Sao Paulo called Chirac's 48-hour trip to Brasilia, Rio and Sao Paulo "France's re-discovery of Brazil" and said it had everything to be a political success.

"There is a good area for agreement between the two countries," it said. "On the one hand Brazil wants to get rid of EU protectionism, on the other France wants to keep supplying equipment to Brazil."

Bilateral trade exchanges have fallen sharply through a long period of neglect, with France letting some of its EU partners take a handsome lead. But French investment in Brazil recovered last year with utility Electricite de France buying the Light power company and Renault building a $1 billion car plant.
Keen to find new markets for a French economy plagued by slow growth and unemployment Chirac is taking some 20 top businessmen to Brazil, which has embarked on a wide privatisation programme.

He is paying tribute to Brazil's national passion, travelling with former French soccer captain Michel Platini, chief organiser of the 1998 World Cup finals in France, and hosting a dinner on Wednesday in Rio for soccer figures including the legendary Pele.
